source: NCI Dictionary of Cancer Terms (National Cancer Institute, US government, public domain); definitions paraphrased and shortened

metastatic.plain: has spread from where it started to other parts of the body

metastasis.plain: the spread of cancer from where it started to other parts of the body

metastases.plain: places the cancer has spread to in the body

adjuvant.plain: treatment given after the main treatment to lower the chance the cancer comes back

neoadjuvant.plain: treatment given before the main treatment, often to shrink a tumor first

randomized.plain: people are put into groups by chance, like flipping a coin

placebo.plain: a pill or treatment with no active medicine in it

double-blind.plain: neither the patients nor the doctors know who gets which treatment

open-label.plain: everyone knows which treatment is being given

relapsed.plain: has come back after getting better

remission.plain: signs of cancer have gone down or gone away

measurable disease.plain: a tumor that can be seen and measured on a scan or exam

gastrointestinal.plain: related to the stomach and intestines

neurologic.plain: related to the brain and nerves

ECOG performance status.plain: a score of how well a person can do daily activities; lower scores mean more active

Karnofsky performance status.plain: a score of how well a person can do daily activities; higher scores mean more active

performance status.plain: a measure of how well a person can do daily activities

informed consent.plain: a person's written agreement to join a study after learning the risks and benefits

protocol.plain: the written plan that explains how a study is done

eligibility.plain: whether a person meets the rules to join a study

inclusion criteria.plain: the rules a person must meet to join a study

exclusion criteria.plain: the reasons a person cannot join a study

chemotherapy.plain: drug treatment that kills cancer cells

radiotherapy.plain: treatment that uses high-energy rays to kill cancer cells

radiation therapy.plain: treatment that uses high-energy rays to kill cancer cells

immunotherapy.plain: treatment that helps the body's immune system fight cancer

targeted therapy.plain: treatment that attacks specific features of cancer cells

hormone therapy.plain: treatment that blocks or lowers hormones that help some cancers grow

systemic therapy.plain: treatment that travels through the blood to reach cancer cells all over the body

biopsy.plain: removal of a small piece of tissue to check for cancer

histologically confirmed.plain: checked under a microscope and shown to be cancer

histologic.plain: related to how tissue looks under a microscope

cytologically.plain: by checking cells under a microscope

carcinoma.plain: cancer that begins in the skin or in tissue that covers organs

sarcoma.plain: cancer that begins in bone or soft tissue

lymphoma.plain: cancer that begins in cells of the immune system

leukemia.plain: cancer of the blood-forming tissue, such as the bone marrow

tumor.plain: a lump or mass of abnormal cells

progression.plain: cancer that is growing or spreading

progression-free survival.plain: the length of time during and after treatment that the cancer does not grow

overall survival.plain: the length of time from the start of treatment that a person is still alive

response rate.plain: the share of people whose cancer shrinks or goes away with treatment

toxicity.plain: harmful side effects of a treatment

adverse event.plain: an unwanted or harmful effect during a study

comorbidity.plain: another health condition a person has at the same time

prior therapy.plain: treatment a person already had before joining

first-line.plain: the first treatment given for a disease

locally advanced.plain: cancer that has grown near where it started but has not spread far

resection.plain: surgery to remove part or all of an organ or tissue

biomarker.plain: a measurable sign in the body that shows what a disease or treatment is doing

antibody.plain: a protein made by the immune system that attaches to a specific target

palliative.plain: treatment meant to ease symptoms rather than cure the disease

curative.plain: treatment meant to cure the disease

life expectancy.plain: how long a person is expected to live

bone marrow.plain: the soft tissue inside bones where blood cells are made

stem cell transplant.plain: a procedure that replaces diseased blood-forming cells with healthy ones

breastfeeding.plain: feeding a baby with breast milk
